title: MicroHub Exercises
text: Use these exercises to practice moving from a public health forecasting question to a MicroHub forecast output.

title: MicroHub Exercises
text: It is January 7, 2026. Produce four-week influenza hospitalization forecasts beginning with the week ending January 10, 2026 using weekly data from February 2022 through January 3, 2026 for Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Maryland, and North Carolina.

previous_headings: MicroHub Exercises > Exercise 1: Influenza Hospitalization Forecasts
title: MicroHub Exercises
text: Download exercise-1-flu-hospitalizations.zip from the Downloads page and unzip it before uploading the CSV to MicroHub. The file includes date target_group population and value.

previous_headings: MicroHub Exercises > Exercise 1: Influenza Hospitalization Forecasts
title: MicroHub Exercises
text: Open MicroHub, upload the exercise CSV, confirm date target_group population and value, set the forecast date to January 7 2026, set a 4-week horizon, select United States for seasonality, run all available forecasting models, compare model plots, create an ensemble forecast, and download the forecast output report and visualization plots.

previous_headings: MicroHub Exercises > Exercise 1: Influenza Hospitalization Forecasts
title: MicroHub Exercises
text: Which states show the clearest increase, which model responds most strongly, where do models disagree, and which forecasts would you share with a public health planning team.

what: Exercise 2: Forecasting with Recent Reporting Anomalies
title: MicroHub Exercises
text: Use weekly target data for three groups to decide how much recent data to exclude before forecasting and compare model sensitivity to reporting anomalies.

previous_headings: MicroHub Exercises > Exercise 2: Forecasting with Recent Reporting Anomalies
title: MicroHub Exercises
text: Cases appear to be increasing in line with expectations for this time of year but recent reported counts appear lower than expected. This may reflect true decreases delayed reporting incomplete data or another anomaly.

previous_headings: MicroHub Exercises > Exercise 2: Forecasting with Recent Reporting Anomalies
title: MicroHub Exercises
text: Download exercise-2-data.zip from the Downloads page and unzip it before uploading the CSVs to MicroHub. The ZIP includes exercise-2-2025-12-15.csv and exercise-2-2024-02-01.csv. Each file includes date target_group population and value.

previous_headings: MicroHub Exercises > Exercise 2: Forecasting with Recent Reporting Anomalies
title: MicroHub Exercises
text: Upload exercise-2-2025-12-15.csv explore visualizations confirm forecast date and seasonal zone try several data-drop settings run each individual model change selected model parameters then repeat with exercise-2-2024-02-01.csv.

previous_headings: MicroHub Exercises > Exercise 2: Forecasting with Recent Reporting Anomalies
title: MicroHub Exercises
text: For each dataset decide how many weeks of data to drop explain how forecasts changed compare model sensitivity to dropped weeks and parameter changes and consider how outbreak-season timing affects confidence.

text: MicroHub local infectious disease forecasting dashboard designed help public health teams generate, compare, export probabilistic forecasts without working directly model source code. built R Shiny application can run locally Docker Desktop. tool supports practical forecasting workflow: Upload surveillance data. Configure real-time forecast settings. Run one individual forecasting models. Compare model plots uncertainty intervals. Build ensemble forecast. Download hub-ready forecast outputs.
